It also asks what the softness might be hiding, and whether going along with things is kindness or a way of never having to hold a line.

Pisces rising adapts and merges and gives people back a flattering reflection of themselves, and it's disarming. The card sees a wish to be liked and needed in that, one that has you dissolving your own edges to fit whatever the moment wants. You'd call it being easy and compassionate. What you may not see is how the lack of a firm no lets people take more than they should, so you end up carrying things that were never yours. You're loved, and you're quietly drained, and people rarely notice the second part.

Starting a new job, it's saying yes to everything and being buried by the third week. In dating it's becoming what the other person wants and disappearing in the process. In a new group it's being everyone's gentle favourite while nobody takes your own needs seriously. Show one firm edge early with someone new, a clear preference about where to eat, a kind no, and let them meet an actual person with opinions.
rising.reversed:
Blurred over, a Pisces Ascendant's soft front loses its shape. You become whatever each person wants, and nobody, yourself included, can find the real you. The sextile offers an edge to stand on and you keep melting past it. The gentleness becomes a way of avoiding any position you might have to defend. Some people find that restful at first, and then can't work out what you want from them.

Colleagues find you agreeable and don't trust you to hold a line. Socially it's a vagueness people find sweet and slightly maddening. On a date it's 'I don't mind, you choose', said so often they stop asking. The next time it comes up, say one clear thing you want, and hold to it when the urge to melt back into agreement rises.

1.upright:
Before you've said a word, people have read your first house. It's the body, how you carry it, and how you begin things, and it's angular, one of the chart's four corners, so whatever turns up here shows. The Devil brings Capricorn into it, and Capricorn squares Aries, the first house's natural sign. That's friction between two cardinal signs, the patient climber and the one who charges, and fire and earth have no natural liking for each other. So the card sits on your self-image a bit awkwardly, which is useful, because it gets noticed.

What it's pointing at is a habit you've started to treat as your personality. The coffee in your hand in every photo. Always having to be the busy one. The gym routine you can't miss without feeling like someone else, or the look that takes an hour every morning and that you'd feel exposed without. None of these are wrong. The card just asks which of them you'd call 'just who I am', and whether that's true, because the Devil works best on things we've stopped seeing as choices. Other people can often see it working on you before you can, since this house faces outward.

In the body it might be tension you carry as posture, the jaw, the shoulders up round your ears. In how you begin things it's a need to prove yourself running under every new start. In how strangers read you it's the one thing they'd mention if asked to describe you. Ask someone who knows you well what habit they'd say defines you, and don't argue with the answer.
1.reversed:
With the card reversed in the first house, the thing you've fused with your identity is usually starting to pinch. The persona doesn't fit as well as it did, the tough one, the party one, the one who's always fine, and you're tired of wearing it. Or you're holding onto it harder precisely because it's slipping, doubling down on the look, the routine, the version of you everyone expects. Capricorn's square to this house means the change tends to come in jolts.

It shows in the body as the strain of holding a shape that doesn't suit you, and in first meetings as armour people can feel. Pick one visible thing you do on autopilot, how you start the day, what you reach for in your first ten minutes, and change it for a month. Pay attention to what you're like without it.

2.upright:
Actual money lives in the second house, and so does the harder thing underneath it, what you think you're worth. It's a succedent house, the kind that builds up and holds, and its natural sign is Taurus, earth like Capricorn, the two in a trine. Venus rules it. So The Devil walks into this room as if it owned the place. Same element amplifies, the good and the too much, and money and possessions are exactly the solid, countable things this card deals in.

The pull here is toward more, and toward keeping. A pay rise that got swallowed by a bigger rent within six months. Buy-now-pay-later instalments that are small on their own and add up to a second car payment. Wardrobes and garages and storage units full of things you maintain, insure and occasionally feel guilty about. Because the house consolidates, whatever starts here tends to stack up, the debt, the stuff, and the habit of measuring yourself against a number. The self-worth side is sneakier. The card likes you to believe you're worth what's in the account, so you keep earning to feel like enough, and enough never quite arrives.

With income it's the job you'd leave tomorrow if the money matched somewhere else. With spending it's the purchase made to settle a mood, usually late in the evening. With possessions it's the things you own that have started to own your weekends. Add up what you pay each month for things you barely use, subscriptions, storage, the second car, and look at the figure for a while before you decide anything.
2.reversed:
Reversed in the second house, the card usually shows money fear running things. You might be checking the banking app several times a day, keeping money you'll never let yourself enjoy, or saying no to anything that costs because some part of you is sure it'll all run out. The other version is spending to quiet the same fear, a new thing for every bad day. Earth on earth gives the worry nothing to interrupt it, so it compounds as quietly as interest.

It shows in the account, obviously, and in the tightness you feel opening a bill. It shows in how you talk about yourself when money's short, as if you'd become less of a person. For one month, note every purchase along with the mood you were in when you made it. The pattern is usually obvious by the second week.

3.upright:
Your phone is probably the best picture of the third house there is. Messages, news, the group chat, the commute, siblings and neighbours, the things you say without thinking and what you pick up along the way. It's a cadent house, where things get processed, and its natural sign is Gemini, ruled by Mercury. Capricorn sits quincunx to Gemini, five signs apart with nothing shared, and earth and air are opposed elements. So The Devil never fits comfortably in this light, busy room. It sits in the middle of your thinking like a heavy piece of furniture you keep walking round.

What's live is the loop. The phone picked up a hundred times a day without deciding to. The news you check because not checking feels irresponsible. The group chat you'd leave if leaving didn't feel like a statement. And the lines you say about yourself so often you've stopped hearing them, 'I'm hopeless with money', 'I'm not a maths person', 'that's just how our family is'. The Moon has its joy in this house, so these habits of mind are emotional too, comforting in their way, which is why they stick. The quincunx means shifting one takes lots of small corrections, and a single big decision rarely does it.

With a sibling it's the old dynamic neither of you questions, who's the clever one, who's the difficult one. With learning it's the belief you're bad at something, kept alive because it saves you trying. Count honestly how many times you pick up your phone in one ordinary day, and write the number somewhere you'll see it.
3.reversed:
The third house reversed tends to show thinking stuck in a groove. The same worry circling on the drive to work, the same argument with a brother replayed word for word years later, the scroll you can't stop even when you're bored of it. Or the words turn sharp, gossip that feels good for ten minutes, the sarcastic message sent before you'd thought, the neighbour you've decided to dislike. The quincunx keeps it all slightly out of joint, so clarity comes and goes.

It shows in sleep, when the loop starts up as soon as the light's off. It shows with siblings and neighbours, where the same small fight keeps happening. Take the app you open most without meaning to and move it off your home screen for a fortnight. Notice what you do with your hands instead.

4.upright:
Capricorn naturally rules the top of the chart, the tenth house, career and public standing. So when The Devil lands in the fourth house, the bottom of the chart, it's sitting at the far end of its own axis, in the room for home, family and roots. Cancer is the fourth's natural sign, ruled by the Moon, and it sits opposite Capricorn. Earth and water are friendly, each feeding the other, so this isn't a hostile placement. It's more that the card looks at your private life with the eyes of the world outside, and asks what's being run on duty.

Home and family are where the oldest habits live. The Sunday lunch you can't skip without a week of guilt. The role you've always had, the peacemaker, the responsible one, the one who's a bit of a disappointment, and still slip into the moment you walk through your parents' door. The house rules you absorbed about money, about drinking, about what gets talked about and what doesn't. Because this is an angular house, whatever binds you here sits under everything else, and it can feel like the floor itself. The mortgage belongs here too, the one that decides which jobs you can say yes to.

At home it might be clutter you can't part with because each thing holds a person. With parents it's the approval you're still working for as an adult. With the place you live it's staying somewhere, a suburb, a town, a house, because leaving would feel like a betrayal. Write down three rules from the house you grew up in that you still follow, and next to each, whether you'd choose it.
4.reversed:
When this card is reversed in the fourth house, a family habit is usually being pressed on. Something nobody talks about, the drinking, the money, the favourite child, the relative everyone tiptoes round, and you can feel either the silence cracking or everyone working very hard to keep it in place. Sometimes the change is yours. You finally stop doing the thing you've always done at home, and the household doesn't know what to do with you.

It shows at family gatherings as tension that starts in the car on the way there. It shows in your own home when you catch yourself saying your mother's words in your mother's voice. Do one family ritual differently, a birthday, a holiday, the regular phone call, and let people have their reaction without talking them out of it.

5.upright:
Pleasure is the fifth house's business. Romance, creativity, children, hobbies, games, anything done for the fun of it, and in older astrology gambling and speculation too. Venus has her joy here. The natural sign is Leo, fixed fire ruled by the Sun, and Capricorn is quincunx to it, five signs off with no common ground, while fire and earth have no natural feeling for each other. The Devil drawn into this room is a sober card at a party, and what it's interested in is which of your fun has turned into something you need.

Things that start as play can harden without you noticing, especially in a succedent house like this one, which holds onto what builds up. The betting app that was a laugh during the footy and is now a habit. The dating apps opened on every bad evening. The person you keep chasing who's never quite available, where the chase is the point. The creative work you can only enjoy if people praise it. With children it might be your own screen time, or theirs, or the way family fun has slid into always being about buying something. It all still feels like fun from inside.

In romance it's attraction to what you can't have, felt as passion. In creative work it's the project that stopped being a pleasure once it had to impress. In leisure it's the weekend that doesn't feel like a weekend without a drink in it. Plan a month of fun that costs nothing and involves no screens or alcohol, and notice which bits you miss and which you don't.
5.reversed:
Fun can go flat when the card is reversed in the fifth house. You go through the motions, the night out, the date, the hobby, and feel oddly empty, because the thing that used to delight you has become a habit you keep up. Or it runs the other way into excess, the spending on treats, the romance that's all thrill and no kindness, the pleasure that leaves you worse every time.

It shows with children as impatience in the moments that are meant to be play. It shows in creative work as a block that turns up whenever you feel watched. Pick one thing you used to love before it became something you had to be good at, and do it badly, privately, for the pleasure of it.

6.upright:
The alarm, the commute, the job you actually do between nine and five, the dishes, the dog, the body kept running. That's the sixth house. Virgo is its natural sign, earth like Capricorn, the two in a trine, so The Devil slots into your routine very easily. Same element amplifies. Mars has its joy in this house, which gives the sixth an appetite for effort, and Capricorn brings its own relentless work ethic. Together they can build a day that works you, instead of one you work in.

This is where habits live in their plainest form. Coffee to get going, something at night to switch off, the phone checked before your feet touch the floor. The workout that used to feel good and now feels like punishment if you miss it. The diet with so many rules you need an app to keep track. Being first in and last out, and quietly proud of it. Because the house is cadent, about adjusting and serving, these patterns sit in the small repeated moments, the ones you stopped deciding about years ago. The card asks which of them you'd keep if you were designing your days from scratch.

In the body it's what you lean on to get through, and what it costs your sleep. At work it's overwork you call being conscientious, and the colleague who's learned they can leave things for you. At home it's chores done to a standard nobody else asked for. Write down one ordinary day hour by hour, and circle the things you'd drop if nobody minded.
6.reversed:
Four coffees where there used to be one. That's the sort of thing the card shows reversed in the sixth house, a routine that's tipped into running you. The gym has become a way to punish yourself for a weekend. You're answering work messages in the bath. Or the routine has fallen apart altogether, meals skipped, sleep all over the place, and you're pushing on regardless because stopping would mean admitting how tired you are. Earth on earth leaves the pattern nothing to break it.

It shows in the body first, the energy that dips mid-afternoon, the stiff back, the headaches. At work it's the job that's crept into your evenings so gradually you never agreed to it. Pick the one daily habit that takes more than it gives, and cut it by half for a month before you decide whether to stop.

7.upright:
Whoever sits across from you in life belongs to the seventh house. A partner, a business partner, anyone you've made a serious agreement with, and sometimes the open rival. It's angular, so what happens here is active and in the foreground. Libra is its natural sign, ruled by Venus, and Capricorn squares Libra, two cardinal signs grinding against each other. Earth against air adds to it, solid terms against the ideal of fairness. The Devil drawn here puts the power in a close relationship on the table.

Every relationship has some deal underneath it, and this card wants to see yours. Who holds the passwords and the money. Who decides where you spend the holidays. Whose moods set the temperature in the house. Whether you stay partly because the rent's in both names, or because you're not sure you'd cope on your own, or because the business depends on you both being in it. None of that makes the relationship false. Plenty of good relationships have practical glue. The square just means that when the deal stops being fair, it doesn't stay quiet, and you'll feel it as friction until someone says it out loud.

With a partner it's the subject you've never been able to raise without an argument. In business it's a contract you signed quickly and now feel bound by. With an ex it's the one you keep going back to, even though you both know how it ends. Write down plainly what you'd lose and what you'd gain if one important partnership ended, and keep the list private.
7.reversed:
Power in a partnership is usually lopsided when this card turns up reversed in the seventh house, and someone's starting to push back. It might be you, finally saying you won't be spoken to that way, or won't be the one who always gives in. It might be them. There can be jealousy, checking up, the silent treatment, or an ex who's suddenly back in your messages. The square to Libra keeps the tension active, so it tends to come to a head.

It shows in arguments that are about the dishes and really about who has the say. It shows in business as a partner who's started treating you like staff. Pick the one pattern between you that you'd most like to change, and ask for the change in one plain sentence, without a list of past examples.

8.upright:
This is the most private room in the chart. The eighth house holds shared money, debts, inheritances, sexual intimacy, and the things that have to end so something else can start. Scorpio is its natural sign, and Capricorn sits sextile to it, a cooperative angle, and earth and water are friendly. So The Devil is at ease here. It's a succedent house, where things build up and hold, which suits a card that's all about what we get tied to.

Money and closeness get tangled in this house. A loan to a family member that's never mentioned and never repaid. A joint credit card one of you uses far more than the other. An inheritance that's turned siblings cold. In intimacy it can be sex used to keep someone close, or a relationship that's mostly physical and hard to leave for exactly that reason. The Devil's concern is power, who has it and who's given it away, and it often shows most clearly in what two people won't talk about. There's also the ending you won't let happen, the relationship or job or grief that finished a long time ago and still has you by the collar.

With shared money it's the debt you'd be embarrassed to say the full figure of. In intimacy it's jealousy, or the fear of being left, steering things where desire should be. With endings it's the thing you keep visiting that finished years ago. List every debt you share with anyone and who knows the real numbers, and give a copy to the person it concerns.
8.reversed:
Shared arrangements go sour quietly, and with the card reversed in the eighth house one usually has, and nobody wants to say so. The joint account with a partner who's started hiding purchases. The family money everyone's circling. A physical relationship that's turned into a way of keeping score. Or an ending you've been putting off is pressing to happen, and holding the door shut takes more strength each month.

It shows in arguments about money that are really about trust, and in a coldness in bed that neither of you names. It shows around a will or an estate. Choose the one shared matter you've avoided, set a time to talk about it properly, and bring the actual figures or facts with you.

9.upright:
Belief, study, travel, the law, and whatever you think your life is for all sit in the ninth house. Its natural sign is Sagittarius, ruled by Jupiter, and Capricorn is the very next sign along, semi-sextile, neighbours with little in common. Sagittarius has the faith, Capricorn has the structure, and each is short of what the other has. Fire and earth are neutral to each other. The Sun has its joy in this house, so it's a place meant for light and for seeing further, and The Devil's question is where you've stopped looking.

This is the placement for beliefs taken on whole. The podcast host whose opinions you've absorbed wholesale. The politics that's turned into a team you support. A faith you left years ago whose rules still decide what you feel guilty about. The qualification you keep adding to because another certificate feels safer than starting the actual work. A fair test is whether you'd still hold the belief if the people you admire dropped it. Because this is a cadent house, belief here should keep moving and adjusting, and when it stops, it starts holding you in place.

In study it's the course taken for the letters after your name. With travel it's the trip that's really an escape, and the restlessness waiting when you get back. With in-laws or anyone from another background, it's the certainty about how things should be done. Read one serious piece by someone who disagrees with you about something that matters to you, and read it to the end.
9.reversed:
A belief is either cracking or being clung to harder when the card sits reversed in the ninth house. You might find yourself arguing more fiercely online about something you're privately less sure of. Or a teacher, a church, a movement you trusted has let you down, and you're not sure what's left if you stop believing. Sometimes it's travel, the move overseas you keep planning as a way out of a life you haven't looked at properly.

It shows in study as a course you can't finish and can't quit. It shows in family arguments that go round the same big topic every holiday. Write down the belief you'd least like to question, and underneath it, the name of the person you got it from.

10.upright:
This is The Devil's own ground. The tenth house is naturally Capricorn's, ruled by Saturn, and the card is Capricorn's Major, so card and house share the same sign, the same element, the same planet. It's also angular, the top of the chart, the most public place there is. Career, reputation, standing, the boss and the institution, what you're known for. Everything this card knows about ambition, status and the price of being on top is at full strength here.

What it looks at is what you'd have to give up to stay where you are. The work phone that means your evenings aren't yours. The title that took ten years and now takes your weekends. The reputation you keep polishing, for being the reliable one, the high performer, the one who never drops a ball, until keeping it up is the actual job. Often there's a parent somewhere in it, a voice that told you early what success looked like, and you've been chasing that picture ever since without checking whether you like it. From outside it looks completely reasonable, and your friends probably envy some of it.

In your career it's the next rung you're reaching for mostly because it's there. With a boss it's the request you can't turn down because you've never turned one down. With reputation it's the version of you on LinkedIn that you're getting tired of maintaining. Ask yourself what you'd do for work if it paid the same and nobody would know the title, and write the first answer down.
10.reversed:
The career question tends to press hard with this card upside down in the tenth house. You might be seeing, clearly and a bit painfully, how much of your working life has been about someone else's idea of success, or about fear of what happens if you stop. Or you've pulled right back, doing the minimum and resenting the job while telling no one you want out. Card and house being the same sign, there's no softening, and the reckoning tends to be blunt.

It shows at work as dread on Sunday evenings, and with the boss as a resentment you can feel in your jaw in meetings. It shows at home when your family gets the tired leftovers of every day. Have one honest conversation about your work with someone who doesn't benefit from you staying, a friend, a mentor, a career counsellor, and say the thing you've been leaving out.

11.upright:
Friends, groups, networks and the online crowd belong to the eleventh house, along with the hopes you've pinned on the future. Its natural sign is Aquarius, next door to Capricorn, and the two share Saturn as their traditional ruler, so The Devil isn't a total stranger here. Earth and air still pull in opposite directions, the solid against the ideal. Jupiter has its joy in this house, which is meant to make it generous and expansive, and the card asks which of your connections are doing that and which are holding you in place.

Belonging is a strong pull, and this card knows how to use it. The Friday drinks you go to because missing them feels like losing your place. The school friends you've outgrown and keep seeing out of loyalty. The follower count you check. The committee you joined for a year and are still on six years later. It's a succedent house, so groups here build up and set, and a network can become an identity you don't know how to leave. Hopes belong here too, and the card is interested in any dream you're chasing that was really someone else's, a parent's, a friend group's, the one everyone your age seems to be having.

With friends it's doing what the group does, drinking, spending, gossiping, because the group does it. Online it's shaping yourself to whatever gets a reaction. With your hopes it's a future you've kept planning for without asking whether you still want it. Think of the last three things you did mainly because your crowd was doing them, and decide which you'd keep.
11.reversed:
A group can end up with too much say, and that's usually what the card means reversed in the eleventh house. You go along with the plan, laugh at the joke you didn't like, spend what everyone else spends, and come home feeling a little less yourself. Or you've pulled right away from people to avoid that, and you're lonelier than you'd admit. The shared Saturn between the house and the card can make friendship feel like obligation, a roster you keep up.

It shows in a group chat that makes you anxious. It shows in money spent on birthdays, weddings and weekends away that you'd never have chosen. Say no to the next group plan you don't want to go to, kindly and without an excuse, and see who checks in with you afterwards.

12.upright:
Sleep, dreams, retreat, the things you do when nobody's watching, and the patterns that trip you up without your quite seeing how, all belong to the twelfth house. Its natural sign is Pisces, and Capricorn sits sextile to it, a friendly opening, with earth and water getting on. There's a neat detail here. Saturn, which rules Capricorn and so rules this card, has its joy in the twelfth. The Devil's own planet is at home in the dark part of the chart, and what that means in practice is that structure and plain honesty work unusually well here.

What's live is the private habit. The phone in bed until two. The spending done in secret, the parcels hidden in the boot of the car. The drink poured when the house is asleep. Or the less visible kind, the way you always leave a job at around eighteen months, the way every relationship falls apart at the same stage, the fear you've never said aloud that keeps choosing for you. Because the house is cadent and hidden, these patterns run in the background, and you find yourself back in the same spot wondering how. Saturn's help here is very ordinary, a regular bedtime, a counsellor you see on the same day each fortnight, a friend who knows.

With sleep it's what you do in the hour before bed. With private habits it's the thing you'd be embarrassed to be walked in on. With the bigger pattern it's the same ending you keep arriving at. Tell one person you trust about a habit you keep hidden, or book a few sessions with a counsellor, and say it out loud to them.
12.reversed:
The private habit usually gets harder to hide when this card lands reversed in the twelfth house, from other people or from yourself. The partner who's noticed the phone kept face down. The credit card statement that doesn't add up. Or it goes the other way and you retreat further, more time alone, more sleep, more nights in, calling it rest when it's closer to hiding. With Saturn at home in this house the pressure is real, and the sextile means help is close if you'll accept it.

It shows in sleep that never quite refreshes you, and in a tiredness you can't explain to people. It shows as the same self-defeating move made at the same point in things. Write down the pattern you keep repeating, where it starts and where it always ends, and give the page to someone who'll ask you about it.
